title: APPENDIX: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY
text:
10        APPENDIX: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY

"Dip into the future, far as human eye could see,
See the vision of the noonday and the wonders that would be."

His talks, while always impromptu, were not only inspirational and uplifting, but were also models of brevity and gems of diction. He was adept at putting his ideas in a few words of crystal clarity, then driving them home with the warm enthusiasm of a true teacher. He could turn enthusiasm, energy and determination into a bunch of boys and girls and get results that few other men could get; and no man living could so fully reproduce in words, gesture and telling effect, just one of those Halsell gems.

But alas! That master builder is with us no more. He has quit the walks of men. He fought a good fight. He kept the faith; he finished his course, and through the years he helped to shape the lives of hundreds of his pupils for the good of all mankind. Knowing him as I did, and admiring him as only a broadly educated man can admire an intellect and a character like his, the day of his departure came; when his frail body, worn out by ceaseless toil in the cause of humanity, was no longer able to function, his restless spirit, instead of "tying to its star" and climbing to meet the dawn, pulled loose from this side of the river of the Stygian river, stepped unhesitatingly into the waiting boat, and was "ferried across" no screen." And on reaching the far side he turned and stood on shore, and seemed to be gazing toward those whom he was leaving behind—his ex-course, his ex-students.

Listen! Even now I seem to hear him calling to us across the rolling tide: "When I was with you at Savoy I told you to look up and not down—to tie your wagon to a star—and to climb, climb. It is time to lay aside every weight which so easily besets you and press on with boldness. Keep on looking up; but no longer ad astra—let your gaze go beyond the stars—ad lucem, out into the full light; because—for the weary traveler and the

L. J. Reynolds,
Class of '87.
